You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

import re

# Try accessing a cached version of ScienceDirect reference works browse page

session.headers.update({
    'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/91.0.4472.124 Safari/537.36'
})

        url = f'https://web.archive.org/web/{ts}id_/https://www.sciencedirect.com/browse/reference-works'
        print(f'Trying {ts}...')
        resp = session.get(url, timeout=10, allow_redirects=True)
        if resp.status_code == 200 and 'sciencedirect' in resp.text.lower():
            # Look for domain/subject data
            text = resp.text
            # Find reference works counts
            matches = re.findall(r'(?:Life Sciences?|Health Sciences?|Physical Sciences?|Social Sciences?)[^<]*?(?:\d+)', text)
            if matches:
                print(f'Found matches with {ts}:')
                for m in matches:
                    print(m)
            # Also look for data attributes
            counts = re.findall(r'data-count="(\d+)"', text)
            names = re.findall(r'data-name="([^"]+)"', text)

                print(f'Names: {names}')
            # Print some content to understand structure
            print(f'Status: {resp.status_code}, Length: {len(text)}')
            # Show a snippet around 'reference works'

            if idx >= 0:

            break
        else:
            print(f'Status: {resp.status_code}, Length: {len(resp.text)}, has sciencedirect: {"sciencedirect" in resp.text.lower()}')

import asyncio
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
import re

async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser = await p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        context = await browser.new_context(
            user_agent='Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/108.0.0.0 Safari/537.36'
        )
        page = await context.new_page()
        
        print('Navigating to ScienceDirect reference works...')
        try:
            await page.goto('https://www.sciencedirect.com/browse/reference-works', timeout=30000, wait_until='networkidle')
            print(f'Page loaded. Title: {await page.title()}')
            
            content = await page.content()
            print(f'Content length: {len(content)}')
            
            # Save full content for analysis
            with open('/app/sd_page.html', 'w') as f:
                f.write(content)
            
            # Look for reference works data
            # Try to find elements with counts
            elements = await page.query_selector_all('*[data-count]')
            print(f'Elements with data-count: {len(elements)}')
            for el in elements[:20]:
                name = await el.get_attribute('data-name') or ''
                count = await el.get_attribute('data-count') or ''
                text = (await el.inner_text()).strip()[:100]
                print(f'  name={name}, count={count}, text={text}')
            
            # Also look for text patterns
            text = await page.inner_text('body')
            with open('/app/sd_text.txt', 'w') as f:
                f.write(text)
            
            # Print lines containing numbers near domain names
            for line in text.split('\n'):
                if re.search(r'(life|health|physical|social|science|reference|count|domain|subject)', line, re.IGNORECASE):
                    if re.search(r'\d+', line):
                        print(f'  LINE: {line.strip()[:200]}')
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f'Error: {e}')
            # Try to get whatever content we have
            try:
                content = await page.content()
                with open('/app/sd_page.html', 'w') as f:
                    f.write(content)
                print(f'Saved partial content: {len(content)} bytes')
            except:
                pass
        
        await browser.close()

asyncio.run(main())
PYEOF
